31265.name: Communication for IT Professionals
31265.description:
This core subject will highlight new ways of working, provide insights into the scope of technology, and look at considerations within the Australian context. You will learn to make decisions that impact people, community, and the environment. Through authentic experiences, you will develop skills and knowledge, providing a solid base for your continuous professional development as an IT professional.

In the subject, you will complete the Engineers Without Borders Challenge, working in a team to develop solutions to real-world challenges for an Australian Aboriginal or Torres Strait Island community. You will form a team with peers, working in and outside class throughout the session on the project that you select. Your team will research the project background, refine scope and identify technological considerations. You will then ideate and prototype potential solutions that work in the community context. Finally, you will propose a fully developed design idea that benefits the partner community.

In completing the challenge, you will develop multidisciplinary and professional skills including:  researching skills to inform the development of design solutions;
applying the design process to solve genuine humanitarian challenges; considering socio-technical issues including working with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities; developing professional communications skill; and participating and leading team processes.

31268.name: Web Systems
31268.description: This subject is an introduction to information technology, using the web as a core case study. You will learn about the underlying hardware, software, networks and operating systems behind websites, and set up a functional website using this knowledge.

31271.name: Database Fundamentals
31271.description: This subject lays the foundation for effective database systems, teaching you how data is structured and managed within organizations, ensuring its usability for applications and users. You will also learn SQL for effective data retrieval and modification, enhancing your ability to work with databases in various contexts.During the subject, you'll explore the significance and challenges of good database design and management, which underpin a strong basis for developing functional software applications. You'll enhance your skills through hands-on practicals and case study analyses, applying theoretical concepts to real-world situations.This subject is particularly beneficial for students pursuing majors in computer science, information systems, or related fields. It prepares you for roles in database administration, software development, and data analysis.

31269.name: Business Requirements Modelling
31269.description: This subject focuses on modelling business requirements, emphasising the importance of understanding different perspectives of the users to enhances system quality in resolving real-world business problems.You'll explore contemporary requirements modelling approaches, both agile and non-agile software engineering principles, methods, tools, and techniques, to analyse business processes and model requirements via the business process models and data models as well as capture functional and non-functional requirements via agile artifacts and object-oriented models.You'll participate in interactive and hands-on lectures, tutorials as well as team projects with real-world business problems, which will develop key skills for critical roles like Business Analyst in designing and developing innovative software systems in professional settings

41092.description: This subject offers a contemporary overview of computer networking, focusing on layered network architecture and the TCP/IP protocol suite, essential for data engineers to understand data transfer across the internet. You'll engage in practical exercises, such as monitoring live network traffic and creating network applications via socket programming. Additionally, you'll gain hands-on experience with Cisco network equipment to construct networks. The subject hones your problem-solving and design skills, enabling you to choose optimal network services and craft applications like web servers and clients for peak data performance.

43030.name: Professional Practice in Computing
43030.description: This subject focuses on tools and techniques used in the professional practice of design, implementation, cybersecurity, and maintenance of computing systems and related software systems. You will gain an understanding of professional standards, codes of conduct, and methodologies for ensuring high quality outcomes in the various domains within which computing systems are employed and how to convey professional progression in these areas.

31272.name: Project Management and the Professional
31272.description:
This subject equips you with project management skills, focusing on information systems and professional project management. You will learn about ethical standards and the organisational context of projects. You will also learn about the roles of project team members,  managing time, risk, cost and communications and the value of quality. These skills are vital for university success and for success in your future career.  

Learning involves being part of a small project team. You will collaborate to create project documents, receiving constructive feedback to foster improvement. These activities culminate in a significant group assessment followed by a reflection on what you have learnt.  
 
You will also write a report stating the possible ethical dilemmas in a given case study and describing how industry codes may be used to suggest solutions to these dilemmas. Academic and professional language and communication skills are measured through a milestone assessment task that gauges both your subject knowledge and communication proficiency.

41039.name: Programming 1
41039.description: This subject provides a foundation in core programming concepts, vital for careers in computer science and software development. It emphasises project-based learning, independent research, and effective communication. You'll also be introduced to real-world programming practices, preparing you to tackle complex industry-level projects. This approach ensures you develop the multifaceted skill set required for solving sophisticated programming challenges.

48023.name: Programming Fundamentals
48023.description: This subject teaches introductory-level Java programming and software design, with no assumed prior knowledge of programming. You will learn about object-oriented programming concepts, data flow, control flow, and basic data structures.

33130.name: Mathematics 1
33130.description: This subject helps you develop the knowledge and skills necessary for problem-solving and mathematical modelling at an introductory level. You will apply differential calculus to model situations in science and engineering that involve oscillations. Integral calculus is used to solve selected problems involving first- and second-order differential equations, and to calculate areas, volumes, lengths and other physical quantities. You will be introduced to vectors, matrix multiplication and determinants, and apply them to problem-solving and modelling. You'll also review sequences and series and be introduced to power series to approximate more functions.

anti_requisite.rule: Anti-requisite rule: (1 AND 2 AND 3 AND 4 AND 5)

37181.name: Discrete Mathematics
37181.description: This subject lays the groundwork for logical reasoning and methodology, crucial for computer science and mathematics students. You’ll tackle the fundamentals of logic, proof techniques, set theory, functions, counting, complexity and correctness of algorithms, and elementary number theory with applications to cryptography.

41040.name: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence
41040.description: This subject enhances your grasp of Artificial Intelligence (AI), covering learning, natural language processing, computer vision, search, knowledge representation, and reasoning. With lectures and practical labs focused on specific AI techniques, you'll learn to select appropriate models and algorithms for tasks and apply AI methods in simple applications. You will be assessed by a knowledge test, a set of mini-AI application examples and a group project addressing a real-world problem using AI technique, reflecting your ability for exemplifying AI applications and designing AI solutions in practical scenarios.

31250.name: Introduction to Data Analytics
31250.description: This subject covers the fundamentals of data analytics, blending art and science to transform large, complex datasets into actionable insights. You will learn data preprocessing, exploration, visualization, and predictive modeling using various data analytics techniques. By connecting cutting-edge research with practical applications, this subject prepares you to undertake data mining projects, collaborate with analytics professionals, and effectively communicate your findings.

33230.name: Mathematics 2
33230.description: This subject is split into multivariate calculus and introductory statistics. You'll develop mathematical skills for modelling systems with multiple variables and learn descriptive statistics, statistical inference, and simple linear regression. Key topics include linear algebra, solving equation sets, eigenvectors and eigenvalues, partial derivatives, optimisation, multiple integrals, probability, particularly in assessing component reliability in engineering.

48024.name: Programming 2
48024.description: This subject teaches concepts, theories and technologies underlying the methods and techniques of OOP programming and GUI programming. You will learn through a combination of lectures, assignments, and practical labs designed to solve real-world problems using Java or Python. The subject will enable you to design, develop and evaluate software systems to meet predefined quality characteristics of functionality (suitability) and usability (understandability, learnability, operability, compliance). By gaining both theoretical understanding and practical skills, you will be equipped to apply all that you have learned to develop and implement the architecture of a business system in various domains.

57304.name: The Ethics of Data and AI
57304.description: This subject addresses the ethical dilemmas surrounding data-driven AI systems in decision-making across various sectors. You will engage in debates on AI's function and development, informed by humanities and social science perspectives. The course emphasises moral and ethical considerations like transparency, fairness, and algorithmic bias, and applies these to real and hypothetical case studies concerning data ethics, regulation, and accountability.

Your learning experience will blend active engagement with real-world applications, particularly in artificial intelligence, preparing you for immediate professional application and further exploration in the field.

41004.name: AI/Analytics Capstone Project
41004.description: This subject culminates your data analytics skills through a team-based project that tackles real-world problems in academia or industry. You'll manage investigations, document progress, and communicate findings. The project encompasses data generation, processing, modelling, analysis, and result interpretation. With an academic mentor's support, your performance is evaluated through written reports and an oral presentation, meeting academic and industry standards.

31243.description: In this subject, you'll engage with a project around data analytics or artificial intelligence. You'll initiate this project in a learning contract, guided by a mentor, to either address a research issue through guided semi-independent research or solve a complex real-world problem by applying practical steps -- data preparation, data preprocessing, pattern discovery/model training, evaluation, and application/deployment, culminating in a detailed report of your findings/solution.This subject equips you with expertise in data analytics/AI techniques and professional communication of results.

42028.name: Deep Learning and Convolutional Neural Network
42028.description: This subject delves into deep learning and convolutional neural networks (CNNs), highlighting their practical applications in data analytics, image recognition, and object detection. You'll study deep learning architectures, focusing on end-to-end model training for tasks like image classification. Practical sessions include setting up deep learning libraries, fine-tuning networks, and training your own CNNs on GPUs. You'll also learn model deployment to build an AI system. The coursework involves individual comprehension of cutting-edge research and collaborative projects to implement image classification and object detection systems.

43023.name: Emerging Topics in Artificial Intelligence
43023.description: This subject offers an introduction to current trends in artificial intelligence (AI), covering areas like machine learning, computer vision, and natural language processing. You'll grasp key concepts, definitions, and algorithms, along with their real-world industry applications. Ideal for those keen on AI research or application development, you'll gain a broad understanding and deep expertise in a specific AI topic through a project mentored by UTS researchers. Your learning will be assessed through reflective exercises, technical implementations, research reports, and oral presentations.

31256.name: Image Processing and Pattern Recognition
31256.description: This subject provides an understanding of image processing and pattern recognition principles, enabling the development of software for automatic image and video analysis. You'll gain skills akin to professional engineers in this field and apply them to real-world problems, like video surveillance detection and automated medical diagnosis, in a team-based project. The aim is to equip you with the ability to scope, solve, test, and communicate solutions effectively.

43024.name: Introduction to Computational Intelligence
43024.description: This subject delves into computational intelligence (CI), including fuzzy logic, neural networks, and evolutionary computation. You'll learn through lectures, assignments, and practical experiments to address real-world issues. Emphasis is on using CI algorithms for problem-solving, knowledge extraction, and model evaluation. You'll understand theories, process data using CI models, and develop validated CI-based solutions for real-world challenges.

41043.name: Natural Language Processing
41043.description: This subject introduces you to Natural Language Processing (NLP), the field that processes and understands human languages. You'll explore core NLP technologies, such as text understanding, machine translation, and sentiment analysis, and apply them to practical problems. The subject offers cutting-edge theories and hands-on techniques, equipping you with the knowledge to embark on NLP research and develop real-world NLP applications.

43008.name: Reinforcement Learning
43008.description: This subject introduces you to reinforcement learning, the study of how machines learn from interactions with their environment. A subset of machine learning, it's essential for automated decision-making and AI, teaching programs to predict and act optimally through experience. You'll explore its applications in control systems, gaming, and inventory management. The subject covers both theory and practice, including Markov Decision Processes, classic and modern algorithms, and hands-on agent training using cutting-edge software tools. By the end, you'll understand value functions, explore exploration versus exploitation, and be able to deploy an AI system to solve real-world problems in your final project.

requisite.rule: Requisite rule: ((1 OR 1a) AND (2 OR 2a) AND (3 OR 3a OR 3b))

41080.name: Theory of Computing Science
41080.description: This subject explores the theory of computation, covering automata, decidability, and computational complexity. These topics provide key tools for you to perform rewriting and parsing, and to determine the complexity of various problems. Understanding computational complexity is crucial for creating cost-effective and practical solutions, such as optimising large-scale problems in online services. Additionally, a firm grasp of computational theory underpins the creation of user-friendly, secure systems and the identification of performance issues in programming, leading to more efficient algorithm design.

40002.name: Architecting on AWS
40002.description: This subject hones your skills in engineering and deploying enterprise-grade applications in the cloud, specifically using AWS. By the end of the subject, you will have acquired the knowledge and skills necessary to become an AWS Certified Solutions Architect (Associate), as the curriculum aligns with the authorized AWS Academy content.

items.details: 41001 Cloud Computing and Software as a Service

40001.name: AWS Industry Studio
40001.description: This studio subject centres on practical application development with AWS, aiming to foster professional competence through a practice-based learning environment for students pursuing an AWS Industry sub-major. You'll engage with reflective design practice, teamwork, mentoring, and deep learning techniques, including architecting and scaling with AWS infrastructure.

41026.name: Advanced Software Development
41026.description: This subject advances your understanding of software development, such as the design, development, and evaluation of a complex software system that fulfills specific functional and non-functional requirements. You will work in highly autonomous teams that, while supervised and directed, take full responsibility for the project and delivery of the expected outcomes. The subject focuses on professional practices including team management, project planning, and all key software development processes. You will also make and justify informed design decisions, enhancing your capability to deliver sound software solutions.

41891.name: Cloud Computing Infrastructure
41891.description: This subject expands on cloud computing, focusing on the setup and operation of cloud infrastructure. You'll explore cloud architecture, virtualisation, storage technologies, data centre basics, and cloud security and compliance. With strong industry relevance, the subject includes practical labs utilising tools prevalent in the cloud infrastructure sector.

41001.name: Cloud Computing and Software as a Service
41001.description: This subject introduces you to cloud computing, covering cloud architecture, IaaS, PaaS, SaaS, virtualisation, and multi-tenancy. You'll engage in group work to produce a research report critically analysing a cloud computing aspect, followed by developing cloud-based software engineering skills on an existing platform. The second assignment involves group collaboration to create a cloud-based software application.

items.details: 42904 Cloud Computing and Software as a Service

requisite.rule: Requisite rule: ((1 OR 1a OR 1b OR 1c OR 1d OR 1e))

41025.name: Introduction to Software Development
41025.description: This subject introduces the fundamentals of modern software development. You will learn agile and non-agile software development principles, methods, tools, and techniques, and explore current trends and challenges in software development. You will also learn how to design, develop, and evaluate software that implements commercially realistic but manageably small requirements. Teaching is delivered through pre-recorded lectures and hands-on workshops. In your weekly workshops and assessment tasks, you will be given assignments to modify or extend existing software features or functions and, at times, to create new ones. You will be encouraged to practice peer learning and collaboration, but ultimately, you must complete your tasks independently. By successfully completing this subject, you will experience, understand the importance of, and be able to apply sound professional practices in software development.

SMJ10188.name: AWS Industry
SMJ10188.description: This sub major aims to empower students with skills in architecting and building applications using Amazon Web Services (AWS). It presents students with skills in building a storage layer, adding a compute layer, database layer and network layer. It then systematically talks about connecting networks, securing user and application access using the AWS platform. Students are taught how to build scalable and fault tolerant applications. It presents students with core cloud services, load balancing and application development. Students who undertake this sub-major will be able to build scalable micro-services using AWS. The taught concepts are supplemented with practical experience in AWS Studios. Students can endeavour to take the AWS certification upon the successful completion of the sub-major.Students must complete 48023 Programming Fundamentals or 41039 Programming 1, 31271 Database Fundamentals and 41092 Network fundamentals or equivalent before commencing this sub-major. It is recommended to complete 41025 Introduction to Software Development. For adding the sub major to UG Engineering courses, only students in Software Engineering major, and possibly Data Science Engineering, and Flexible Engineering can do the sub major.Most students will need to select 41001 Cloud Computing and Software as a Service under options as this is a pre-requisite for 40002 Architecting on AWS; however, students who have already completed 41001 can choose an alternative option.

99200.name: Intercultural Communication

You'll be prepared for the interpersonal and dynamic nature of working in increasingly globalised workplaces and intercultural environments. You'll use a problem-based approach to critically examine numerous frameworks and theories that allow you to interpret intercultural encounters in praxis-based scenarios. You'll apply specific intercultural communication strategies and approaches for their relevance to industry, communities, workplaces and society more broadly.

43029.name: Introduction to Humanitarian Engineering
43029.description: Humanitarian engineering is the application of engineering skills and approaches to enable basic needs and contribute to social justice, with contexts ranging from community and technology development to emergency disaster response, both domestically and internationally. This subject equips you with skills transferable to all engineering fields, including stakeholder engagement, cross-cultural work, human-centred design, and environmental stewardship.You'll build on prior experiences from the Engineers without Borders Challenge, learning about international development, effective humanitarian engineering practices, and key agencies in the field. 95007.name: TD: Pathways to societal transitions
95007.description: Artificial Intelligence seems to be everywhere – embedded in phones, homes, workplaces – but what are the physical infrastructures that make it possible, and how are they reshaping communities and our environment? This subject takes students beyond the screen to investigate the hidden, material side of AI. From data centres and fibre-optic cables to the vast demands for energy, water, and land, students will explore how rapidly expanding digital infrastructure is transforming communities and environments globally, and in their own backyard.Students will hear from a diversity of industry experts working across sectors who are making digital infrastructure expansion possible, and learn how the challenges and opportunities this expansion presents affect sustainability efforts globally, and in Australia. In multidisciplinary teams, students will investigate how digital infrastructure expansion is unfolding in their local community and codesign future scenarios that balance environmental priorities with societal demand for AI. Through this process, they will use a range of ethnographic and creative research methods, including photography, video, and story-making, to learn from their local community and communicate possible futures. This process will be assisted through regular engagements with our industry partner, Lane Cove Council, who will provide first-hand insights into how digital infrastructure expansion is shaping their community.Students participating in this subject will develop skills and confidence in understanding and responding to complex, real-world challenges in multidisciplinary teams, using effective systems approaches to change-making. It is relevant to students from all disciplines including (but not limited to) computer and data science, social sciences, fine arts, communications, science, law and medicine.

95009.name: TD: Change-making for social impact
95009.description: How can we transform ourselves and the systems we live in? This subject invites students to explore the deep connection between personal transformation and systemic change. Through embodied, reflective, and collaborative learning, students engage with practices from mindfulness, complexity science, implementation science, decolonial thinking, and First Nations and other diverse knowledge systems. Across two integrated phases—self-transformation and systems evolution—students learn to sit with the discomfort of change within complex systems, understand the roots of suffering and injustice, and take ethical action in response to real-world challenges co-designed with our industry partner Stockland. Through creative, non-written assessments, students map their inner shifts, design micro-interventions within complex systems, and showcase ripple effects of their work through ritual, installation, and action pledges. Learning flows between immersive in-person sessions, interactive online sessions, and reflective practices, supporting students to build purposeful, relational, and sustainable approaches to social impact within the communities they care about.

977917.name: In-country Contemporary Society Study
977917.description: This subject consists of an international study program with a UTS and coursework (two online seminars) at UTS. This subject provides you with the opportunity to develop your intercultural awareness, and sociocultural knowledge through an international study program with an international UTS partner organisation. It is offered in July and Summer sessions with some varying programs. You will also attend two online seminars at UTS before the start of your international program, as well as after returning from your international program to support your learning experience. The international program includes classroom-based or virtual seminars. The subject focuses on improving your intercultural communication skills and developing a cultural awareness of the multi-dimensional nuanced nature of culture. The collaborative and reflective learning activities during the coursework will allow you to develop your intercultural capabilities via critical thinking through the understanding of your own culture and others. The assessments will require your critical and reflection skills through theoretical and methodological approaches. With the knowledge, values, and skills that you have gained through this course, you will be able to apply them in your professional life. To enrol, firstly, you must be accepted into an approved international program such us UTS Global Short Programs and other pre-approved Faculty led international activities. Secondly, you need to provide the confirmation of your acceptance when you submit your eRequest.

From data centres and fibre-optic cables to the vast demands for energy, water, and land, students will explore how rapidly expanding digital infrastructure is transforming communities and environments globally, and in their own backyard.Students will hear from a diversity of industry experts working across sectors who are making digital infrastructure expansion possible, and learn how the challenges and opportunities this expansion presents affect sustainability efforts globally, and in Australia. In multidisciplinary teams, students will investigate how digital infrastructure expansion is unfolding in their local community and codesign future scenarios that balance environmental priorities with societal demand for AI. Through this process, they will use a range of ethnographic and creative research methods, including photography, video, and story-making, to learn from their local community and communicate possible futures. This process will be assisted through regular engagements with our industry partner, Lane Cove Council, who will provide first-hand insights into how digital infrastructure expansion is shaping their community.Students participating in this subject will develop skills and confidence in understanding and responding to complex, real-world challenges in multidisciplinary teams, using effective systems approaches to change-making. items.description: This subject consists of an international study program with a UTS and coursework (two online seminars) at UTS. 41181.name: Information Security and Management
41181.description: This subject focuses on training you in IT security policy development and human security management while addressing critical legal and ethical considerations. You will lay the groundwork for applying cyber safety and security measures at a corporate level. By conducting security assessments within business constraints, you will learn to employ professional methodologies effectively. The subject also covers the systematic evaluation of business and security operations, equipping you with skills in contingency planning, risk assessment, risk management, and compliance across diverse business environments. You'll be prepared to develop comprehensive security policies and manage human factors in cybersecurity, ensuring robust protection and ethical governance within organisations.

requisite.rule: Requisite rule: ((1 OR 1a OR 1b OR 1c OR 1d OR 1e OR 1f) AND (2 OR 2a OR 2b OR 2c))

48730.name: Cybersecurity
48730.description: This subject equips you with vital cybersecurity skills, addressing the dual aspects of people management and technology to mitigate risks like legal repercussions, financial losses, and eroded trust. You'll develop a robust understanding of cyber-attacks, defense mechanisms, and security services—confidentiality, integrity, availability. You'll also gain hands-on experience with industry-standard technologies such as IPSec, SSL, PGP, and S/MIME. Through practical application, you'll be prepared to enhance the cybersecurity posture of contemporary organisations.

requisite.rule: Requisite rule: ((1 OR 1a OR 1b OR 1c OR 1d OR 1e)) AND ((2 OR 2a OR 2b))

41180.name: Data Analytics in Cybersecurity
41180.description: Data Analytics for Cybersecurity equips you with the skills to leverage big data and threat intelligence in combating both insider and external cyber threats. You will learn to apply statistical methods to discern patterns and use intelligent technologies to identify security issues from data. The subject introduces machine learning applications in cybersecurity and standard data analytics processes. Through hands-on exercises, you will develop practical skills in analysing corporate computer and network vulnerabilities, thereby enhancing your ability to identify and mitigate security risks. This subject bridges the gap between data analytics and cybersecurity, providing you with the tools to effectively protect modern digital infrastructures.

41185.name: Emerging Topics in Cybersecurity and Privacy
41185.description: This subject delves into contemporary IT security theories and practical skills in the cybersecurity profession, enhanced by guest lectures and workshops. You will develop a professional understanding of cybersecurity by examining emerging threats to web applications and systems, along with cutting-edge privacy and ethical issues. You'll explore current trends and challenges through professional practice and literature review. Working in small teams, you'll apply modern techniques for requirements elicitation, analysis, modelling, specification, and validation to real-world projects.

41183.name: Privacy Preserving
41183.description: In this subject you'll master techniques for safeguarding data privacy, enabling organisations to handle personal or confidential data responsibly. The subject explores privacy models to build defenses against privacy breaches, delving into data anonymisation, statistical privacy approaches, and differential privacy, ensuring you can protect and manage sensitive information effectively.

41184.name: Secure Programming and Penetration Testing
41184.description: This subject will equip you with the knowledge and skills necessary to develop secure software and assess the security of systems through source code analysis and penetration testing techniques. There will be coverage of the principles and practices of secure coding, the identification and mitigation of vulnerabilities, software verification, and the methodologies used in penetration testing. You will learn how to approach and develop automatic auditing systems, identifying vulnerabilities and developing security analysis and testing methods to protect systems against cyber-attacks. Additionally, you'll have the chance to engage in national and international security challenges, with assessments on secure programming, software analysis, and your communication skills in speaking and writing.

41182.name: System Security
41182.description: This subject provides a comprehensive understanding of contemporary system security concepts, strategies, and practical techniques essential for securing operating systems, databases, and servers. You will learn to implement security measures throughout the design and configuration phases, ensuring robust system security and privacy. The subject places a strong emphasis on system hardening mechanisms and prominent security techniques, which you will apply in hands-on practical sessions. By testing the resilience of hardened systems against various attack vectors, you will gain critical skills in defending against real-world cybersecurity threats. This subject fosters both theoretical knowledge and practical expertise, preparing you to effectively safeguard corporate computing environments.

976451.name: Contemporary Spain

In the other weeks, the subject focuses on divergent and historical ways of conceptualising Spain. You will learn about important moments in Spain’s history, such as the unification, the Second Republic, the Civil War, the Franco dictatorship, the restoration of democracy, and the sociopolitical developments of recent decades. You will delve into the diversity of national and cultural identities (regionalisms), plurilingualism, gender, film, music, art, migration, economics, and the evolving socio-cultural aspects of contemporary Spain. This subject will also provide you with an understanding of some of the current challenges that the country faces and how a Spanish citizen thinks and feels in the twenty-first century. The collaborative and reflective learning activities will allow you to develop your intercultural capabilities via critical thinking on Spain's diverse and dynamic culture(s), as well as an international perspective. In the assessments, you will apply your critical and reflection skills to identify and analyse contemporary Spain, through theoretical and methodological approaches.

items.name: Contemporary Spain
items.description: This subject introduces you to contemporary Spain through its historical, political, cultural, social, and economic dimensions from a local, national, continental, and global context. You will be provided with the critical skills to identify, reflect, and analyse major current socio-cultural challenges that shape contemporary Spain through the learning of theoretical and methodological approaches for engaging you in intercultural research. In weeks 2 and 12, you will follow an umbrella program shared by all contemporary European society subjects that introduces general issues relating to contemporary Europe: definitions, geographical space, addressing its identity, unification, internal divisions, colonialism, and the impact of migration, among others. In the other weeks, the subject focuses on divergent and historical ways of conceptualising Spain. You will learn about important moments in Spain’s history, such as the unification, the Second Republic, the Civil War, the Franco dictatorship, the restoration of democracy, and the sociopolitical developments of recent decades. You will delve into the diversity of national and cultural identities (regionalisms), plurilingualism, gender, film, music, art, migration, economics, and the evolving socio-cultural aspects of contemporary Spain. This subject will also provide you with an understanding of some of the current challenges that the country faces and how a Spanish citizen thinks and feels in the twenty-first century. The collaborative and reflective learning activities will allow you to develop your intercultural capabilities via critical thinking on Spain's diverse and dynamic culture(s), as well as an international perspective. In the assessments, you will apply your critical and reflection skills to identify and analyse contemporary Spain, through theoretical and methodological approaches.

items.name: Contemporary Spain
items.description: This subject introduces you to contemporary Spain through its historical, political, cultural, social, and economic dimensions from a local, national, continental, and global context. You will be provided with the critical skills to identify, reflect, and analyse major current socio-cultural challenges that shape contemporary Spain through the learning of theoretical and methodological approaches for engaging you in intercultural research. In weeks 2 and 12, you will follow an umbrella program shared by all contemporary European society subjects that introduces general issues relating to contemporary Europe: definitions, geographical space, addressing its identity, unification, internal divisions, colonialism, and the impact of migration, among others. In the other weeks, the subject focuses on divergent and historical ways of conceptualising Spain. You will learn about important moments in Spain’s history, such as the unification, the Second Republic, the Civil War, the Franco dictatorship, the restoration of democracy, and the sociopolitical developments of recent decades. You will delve into the diversity of national and cultural identities (regionalisms), plurilingualism, gender, film, music, art, migration, economics, and the evolving socio-cultural aspects of contemporary Spain. This subject will also provide you with an understanding of some of the current challenges that the country faces and how a Spanish citizen thinks and feels in the twenty-first century. The collaborative and reflective learning activities will allow you to develop your intercultural capabilities via critical thinking on Spain's diverse and dynamic culture(s), as well as an international perspective. In the assessments, you will apply your critical and reflection skills to identify and analyse contemporary Spain, through theoretical and methodological approaches.

32567.description: This subject delves into business intelligence (BI), a comprehensive term encompassing architectures, tools, databases, analytics, applications, and methodologies aimed at facilitating interactive data access and empowering managers to make informed decisions. It introduces decision support systems (DSS), which are computer-based systems combining models, methods, and data to tackle semi-structured or unstructured decisions, demanding user involvement and a user-friendly interface. As high-level business decisions often fall into these categories and are data-intensive, DSS are increasingly integrated with BI techniques for enhanced problem-solving. You'll learn about various aspects of BI and DSS, including group and intelligent support systems, web-based systems, decision optimisation, and personalised recommender systems. Additionally, the subject teaches the design, implementation, and integration of BI techniques to bolster business decision-making processes.

42177.description: This subject imparts the ability to extract information from images and videos using image processing and pattern recognition techniques, underpinning innovative applications like video surveillance and medical diagnostics. You will learn the principles of image processing and pattern recognition, create software for automatic image and video analysis, and explore recent advancements in the field. Your task is to conduct research and project development in a team that hones your ability to articulate a research question or a problem statement, relate it to existing work, select appropriate methods or models, iteratively develop the solution, and effectively present your findings and demonstrate your ability to work as part of a team.You will tackle a real-world problem and develop a complete solution in the project that encompasses stages from background research, through data handling, to solution development and deployment. structure.structure_details: Complete all of the following subjects:

items.name: Reinforcement Learning
items.description: This subject introduces you to reinforcement learning, the study of how machines learn from interactions with their environment. A subset of machine learning, it's essential for automated decision-making and AI, teaching programs to predict and act optimally through experience. You'll explore its applications in control systems, gaming, and inventory management. The subject covers both theory and practice, including Markov Decision Processes, classic and modern algorithms, and hands-on agent training using cutting-edge software tools. By the end, you'll understand value functions, explore exploration versus exploitation, and be able to deploy an AI system to solve real-world problems in your final project.

The coursework involves individual comprehension of cutting-edge research and collaborative projects to implement image classification and object detection systems.
